segments.text: ALERT! Our city council is giving out FAKE relief goods to flood victims!
An unnamed city official stated that the distributed items were 'expired and unsafe for consumption.'
segments.explanation: Vague attribution: Which official? Real alerts name the source.

segments.text: Share this now before more people get hurt!

verifiedSources.name: Official City Council Page
verifiedSources.text: "No relief goods have been distributed yet. Distribution starts tomorrow."

verifiedSources.name: Local News
verifiedSources.text: No reports of expired goods in this area.

segments.text: ALERT! National State University is opening 50 FREE scholarship slots for incoming students!
segments.explanation: The university name is real, but scammers often use real institutions to build trust.

segments.text: To secure your slot, applicants must first send a $50 'processing fee' to CashApp tag $UniScholarships.
segments.explanation: Real scholarships never ask for a processing fee via personal mobile wallets.

segments.text: Please complete your application early as slots are limited.
PM us your receipt. No official website link available at the moment.

verifiedSources.name: Official University Website
verifiedSources.text: "We do not ask for CashApp processing fees. All scholarship applications are processed through our official portal."

verifiedSources.name: Scam Alert Database
verifiedSources.text: CashApp tag $UniScholarships has been flagged multiple times for 'Advance Fee' fraud.

segments.text: Have you tried this new miracle cure?
Even a famous actor swears by it!
segments.explanation: The celebrity's name is correctly used, but their endorsement is entirely fabricated.

segments.text: "I was struggling with high blood sugar until I found GlucoCure Max. It completely reversed my diabetes in 2 weeks!"
segments.explanation: The quote is entirely fabricated and doesn't appear on any of his official channels.

segments.text: This herbal supplement is popular right now.
Buy it now exclusively at this unverified Shopify link: buy-gluco-max-now.shop.co

verifiedSources.name: Celebrity Official Page
verifiedSources.text: "I am not endorsing any diabetes supplement. Please beware of fake ads using my name."

verifiedSources.name: National Health Database
verifiedSources.text: 0 results found for "GlucoCure Max". Not a registered food or drug product.

segments.text: Due to the incoming Super Typhoon,
segments.explanation: The typhoon itself is a real, ongoing weather event. Flagging the typhoon is wrong, only the suspension claim is fake.

segments.text: all classes (all levels) and government work in the region are SUSPENDED tomorrow.
segments.explanation: No matching post exists on the official government social media account.

segments.text: Please share this to everyone in our community!
Stay safe and stay indoors! Share to inform others.

verifiedSources.name: Official Gov PIO Page
verifiedSources.text: "No suspension of classes has been announced yet. We are monitoring the weather."

verifiedSources.name: Memo Database
verifiedSources.text: Memo No. 45-B was issued last year for a completely different event.

segments.text: WORK FROM HOME: Earn $500 to $1,000 daily by just watching YouTube videos!
We are hiring 100 people today for immediate start. No experience needed!
segments.explanation: While 'no experience needed' is common, the ridiculous pay rate for watching videos is the real red flag.

segments.text: To get your starting kit and portal access, pay the $25 training fee via CashApp.
segments.explanation: Legitimate employers will never ask you to pay a fee to start working.

segments.text: DM us your resume to apply!

verifiedSources.name: Labor Dept Advisory
verifiedSources.text: "Beware of online job offers asking for training fees or equipment fees. This is a common scam."

verifiedSources.name: Scam Alert
verifiedSources.text: Shortened links in job offers are highly suspicious and often lead to phishing sites.

segments.text: SECURITY ALERT for all Global Bank Account Holders.
Your account has been temporarily locked due to suspicious login attempts from overseas.
segments.explanation: Banks do lock accounts for suspicious activity, but the method of notification here is fake.

segments.text: Please update your security settings.
Click here to unlock your account: www.globalbank-security-unlock.com
segments.explanation: This is a fake domain. Official Global Bank alerts direct you to the official app or globalbank.com.

verifiedSources.name: Official Bank Advisory
verifiedSources.text: "We will never ask you to click a link to unlock your account or verify your identity."

verifiedSources.name: Domain Check
verifiedSources.text: 'globalbank-security-unlock.com' was registered 2 days ago.

segments.text: I am giving away $10,000 to the first 500 people who share this post!
Congratulations to our previous winners who already received their cash!
segments.explanation: Scammers often use fake testimonials or fake previous winners to build trust.

segments.text: Message our admin 'Jimmy' directly to claim your prize.
segments.explanation: Real giveaways do not require you to message a random admin account.

segments.text: Winners must pay a small $30 transfer fee to receive the $10,000.
segments.explanation: A legitimate giveaway will never ask the winner to pay a fee to receive their prize.

verifiedSources.name: MrBeast Official
verifiedSources.text: "I do not have a separate regional giveaway page. My only official giveaways are on my main verified accounts."

verifiedSources.name: Scam Alert
verifiedSources.text: Requiring a 'transfer fee' or 'tax fee' is the defining characteristic of an advance-fee scam.

segments.text: Bitcoin is crashing, but my students are making millions in passive income!
segments.explanation: The market context might be true, but it's being used to sell a scam.

segments.text: Our new AI trading bot guarantees a 500% return on your investment in just 3 days.
segments.explanation: No legitimate investment can guarantee a 500% return in 3 days. This is mathematically impossible without massive risk.

segments.text: Fully licensed and approved by the SEC and National Bank.
segments.explanation: Checking the SEC database reveals this entity is NOT registered or licensed to solicit investments.

segments.text: Only 5 slots left for the VIP tier! DM me 'INVEST' now.

verifiedSources.name: SEC Advisory
verifiedSources.text: "The entity 'Crypto Wealth Coach' is NOT registered with the Commission and is NOT authorized to solicit investments from the public."

verifiedSources.name: Financial Experts
verifiedSources.text: Guaranteed high returns in a short period are the primary red flag of a Ponzi scheme.

segments.text: Please help! Baby Angel needs an emergency liver transplant within 48 hours or she won't survive.
The hospital bill is already at $200,000 and the doctors are threatening to stop treatment.
segments.explanation: Hospitals in most regions cannot legally deny emergency life-saving treatment due to inability to pay (Emergency Medical Act).

segments.text: We are begging for your kind hearts. Please send any amount to this CashApp: $HelpBabyAngel (Name: J. Cruz).
segments.explanation: The name on the CashApp account does not match the parents' names and the photo is stolen from a 2018 news article in another country.

segments.text: God bless everyone who shares and donates!
segments.explanation: Scammers use religious or moral appeals to lower people's critical thinking.

verifiedSources.name: Reverse Image Search
verifiedSources.text: The photo of the baby was taken from a news article in Brazil from 2018.

verifiedSources.name: Hospital Statement
verifiedSources.text: "We do not have a patient named 'Baby Angel' currently admitted in our pediatric ICU."

segments.text: $1 FLIGHT ALERT! ✈️
Celebrate our anniversary with $1 base fares to ANY domestic destination!
segments.explanation: Piso fares are real promotions, making this scam highly believable.

segments.text: This secret promo is only available through our partner travel agency link, not the main website.
segments.explanation: Airlines host their major sales directly on their official website or app to drive traffic, not exclusively through unknown partners.

segments.text: Book within the next 2 hours before seats run out! Click here: www.1dollar-oceanic-flights-2024.net
segments.explanation: The link points to an unofficial domain designed to steal credit card details.

verifiedSources.name: Official Airline Page
verifiedSources.text: "All our official seat sales are announced and booked exclusively through oceanicairlines.com. Beware of fake pages."

verifiedSources.name: Domain Check
verifiedSources.text: The domain '1dollar-oceanic-flights-2024.net' is not owned by the airline.

segments.text: URGENT: Major Telecom provider just suffered a massive data breach!
Over 5 million customer records, including passwords, have been leaked online.
segments.explanation: While data breaches happen, the claim here is unverified and used to drive panic.

segments.text: According to an anonymous insider, the company is covering it up.
segments.explanation: No cybersecurity firm or news outlet has corroborated this massive claim.

segments.text: Check if your number was compromised by entering it at: telecom-breach-check.xyz
segments.explanation: This is a fake domain designed to harvest active phone numbers.

verifiedSources.name: Official Telecom Page
verifiedSources.text: "We have not experienced any data breaches. Our systems are secure."

verifiedSources.name: National Privacy Commission
verifiedSources.text: No reports of a data breach from the said Telecom provider.

TACTIC_DESCRIPTIONS.Vague Attribution: Citing unnamed or generic sources (e.g. 'an official') to avoid verification.
TACTIC_DESCRIPTIONS.Artificial Urgency: Creating fake time pressure (e.g. 'hurry', 'ends tonight') to rush decisions.
TACTIC_DESCRIPTIONS.Phishing Link: Using deceptive URLs that look official but steal your information.
TACTIC_DESCRIPTIONS.Advance Fee Fraud: Asking for an upfront payment or processing fee for a 'free' reward.
TACTIC_DESCRIPTIONS.Unofficial Domain: Directing users to sketchy, non-official websites or personal messages.
TACTIC_DESCRIPTIONS.Fabricated Quote: Inventing fake statements and attributing them to celebrities or authority figures.
TACTIC_DESCRIPTIONS.Unregistered Product: Selling items claiming health benefits without FDA approval or registration.
TACTIC_DESCRIPTIONS.Suspicious Storefront: Using unverified, temporary e-commerce sites to sell dubious products.
TACTIC_DESCRIPTIONS.Unverified Claim: Making bold, official-sounding statements without any supporting evidence.
TACTIC_DESCRIPTIONS.Fabricated Memo: Referencing fake official documents or memo numbers to appear legitimate.
TACTIC_DESCRIPTIONS.Impersonation: Pretending to be a trusted entity like a bank, company, or government agency.
TACTIC_DESCRIPTIONS.Too Good to Be True: Offering extravagant rewards for minimal effort.
TACTIC_DESCRIPTIONS.Emotional Manipulation: Exploiting fear, pity, or tragedy to bypass critical thinking.
